name: Neopopulism
summary: Neopopulism, in its best-documented scholarly sense, is a political strategy in which a personalistic leader wins direct, unmediated support from large numbers of mostly unorganised followers while enacting market-oriented reform. Its leaders cast themselves as outsiders rescuing the country from crisis, attack established elites and organised interests such as unions, and pair drastic liberalisation and privatisation with targeted anti-poverty programmes. The label is also applied more loosely to 21st-century right-wing anti-establishment movements.
scope: The profile represents Latin American neoliberal neopopulism of the late 1980s and 1990s as analysed by Kurt Weyland and Kenneth Roberts, centred on Carlos Menem in Argentina, Alberto Fujimori in Peru and Fernando Collor in Brazil, with Argentina's State Reform Law 23.696 as the programmatic anchor. Where the sources describe later right-wing neopopulism (Meloni, Orban, Trump, Bolsonaro), that is used only for social and immigration questions and marked low confidence. It excludes classical populism (Peron, Vargas) and left-wing Pink Tide populism.

keyFigures.name: Alberto Fujimori

keyFigures.name: Carlos Menem
keyFigures.role: President of Argentina 1989-1999, cited by Weyland and the Populism Studies glossary as a paradigm neoliberal neopopulist.

sources.title: Ley 23.696, Reforma del Estado (1989)
sources.author: Argentine Congress, via Presidencia de la Nacion
sources.usedFor: Programme of the Menem government: emergency declaration, privatisation of utilities and state firms, worker share programme.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Neopopulist reformers paired adjustment with targeted anti-poverty programmes rather than universal entitlements, and nothing in the sources addresses health coverage, so the answer is a split inference.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Fujimori quadrupled the minimum wage at the start of his term while neoliberal advisers held wages down elsewhere, so adherents are split and the sources do not settle it.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Neopopulist leaders such as Menem and Fujimori embraced drastic market reform, and Argentina's Law 23.696 puts state enterprises up for sale to private capital.

public-ownership.rationale: Law 23.696 declares utilities and energy firms such as YPF, Gas del Estado and SEGBA subject to privatisation, and Fujimori sold hundreds of state enterprises.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Neoliberal neopopulism courted business sectors and focused on raising revenue broadly while shrinking the state; higher wealth taxes are inferred to be disfavoured, not documented.

unions-good.rationale: Weyland says neopopulists keep distance from trade unions as fetters on presidential autonomy and weaken them through labour flexibilisation.

property-fundamental.rationale: Privatisation and the market model rest on secure private property, though personalistic leaders were willing to override rules when convenient.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Market reform meant deregulation, removal of price controls and easing limits on investment, so tighter corporate regulation runs against the programme.

cut-welfare.rationale: Adherents shrank the state but also funded targeted emergency anti-poverty programmes to hold mass support, so they are split on cutting welfare and the sources give no direct line.

worker-ownership.rationale: Law 23.696 let workers buy shares in privatised firms through a participatory-ownership programme, but only as minority stakes inside private firms; collective worker control is not a goal. Inferred.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Personalistic leaders such as Fujimori justified strong security measures against insurgency; the sources do not discuss surveillance, so this is inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: No source states a drug position; security-minded, socially cautious leaders are inferred to oppose legalisation.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Inferred: anti-institutional leaders hostile to speech limits and to elite-imposed norms; not documented in the sources.

strong-leader.rationale: Weyland defines neopopulism as a personalistic leader with direct, unmediated support who concentrates power and shows limited respect for institutional rules.

state-harmful.rationale: Neopopulists shrank the state and attacked rent-seeking, but still used concentrated state power to push reform, so they stop short of calling it harmful in itself.

limit-guns.rationale: The sources never discuss guns and adherents differ by country, so the answer is neutral by inference.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred from Fujimori's security focus and leaders' reliance on the state's coercive arm; not directly documented.

decide-locally.rationale: Neopopulism is plebiscitary and anti-organisational, concentrating power in the national leader rather than devolving it.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from a security-and-order outlook; the sources do not address prison policy.

traditional-family.rationale: Right-leaning neopopulists such as Meloni and Orbán in the broad usage stress family values; for the 1990s core this is inferred.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed for the Latin American core; inferred from socially conservative leaders like Menem and from right-wing neopopulists generally.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from socially conservative leaders; the sources do not state this position.

more-religion-public.rationale: Inferred; leaders like Menem and Bolsonaro courted religious constituencies, but the sources do not document this.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed; right-wing neopopulists reject identity-based redress, but this is an inference.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed in sources; inferred from socially conservative profile.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The glossary notes developed-country neopopulism leans on nationalism, and the Wikipedia article links it to anti-immigrant nativism.

gradual-change.rationale: Neopopulists favoured bold, transformative shock reform and bypassed institutions, so gradualism respecting institutions is disfavoured.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The Wikipedia article describes xenophobic, anti-immigration policies among neopopulist parties, though the Latin American 1990s core says little about it.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: They accepted IMF and World Bank adjustment programmes but also rely on nationalist rhetoric, so adherents are split.

free-trade.rationale: Fujimori abandoned protectionism and import substitution and radically simplified tariffs, a typical neoliberal neopopulist programme.

nation-first.rationale: Neopopulism pairs nationalist rhetoric with openness to global markets and finance, so adherents are split.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Foreign policy is not discussed in the sources, and adherents have no common line.

open-borders.rationale: Neopopulist parties are described as hostile to immigration, which is incompatible with eventual open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Neopopulism is organised around restoring growth and exports through market reform, so limiting growth is contrary to it.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from pro-growth economics and the sceptical posture of leaders like Bolsonaro and Trump.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: No source addresses it and adherents do not share a view.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Energy technology is not addressed; no common position.

revolution-justified.rationale: Neopopulists present themselves as transforming the status quo, but within electoral politics; revolution itself is inferred as rejected.

experts-over-public.rationale: Weyland describes an alliance of neoliberal technocrats with plebiscitary leaders: expert advice drives economics while legitimacy comes from the mass, so adherents are split.

central-planning.rationale: The whole project is to dismantle state-led development and sell state enterprises.

socialized-markets.rationale: Law 23.696 allowed worker share programmes inside privatised firms but treated private capital as the main route; public or worker ownership as the condition for markets is not their position.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed; reform focused on simplifying and raising revenue conventionally. Inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from market-friendly, business-courting economics; not documented.

basic-income.rationale: They favoured targeted programmes for the poor, which Weyland documents, over universal unconditional transfers; basic income itself is inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Fujimori's government abandoned protectionism and simplified tariffs; though Trump-style neopopulists differ, the core profile opposes protective tariffs.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Neoliberal neopopulism rejects state-led development in favour of private investment and market signals.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Fujimori drew on De Soto's property-titling ideas but privatisation also favoured large business groups; adherents are split.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Neopopulism sits inside market capitalism and does not question wage labour; the answer is a strong inference from its market programme.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Neoliberal reforms usually strengthened monetary stability institutions, so abolition is inferred as disfavoured; not documented.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Weyland says neopopulists bypass and marginalise unions and organised interest groups rather than negotiate through state-recognised bodies.

one-party-rule.rationale: Leaders relied on personal vehicles, not a guiding-ideology party, and Weyland notes low institutionalisation; they still ran in elections.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Inferred: plebiscitary, republican leaders; the sources do not address monarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: They won through elections but often bypassed institutions, Fujimori closed Congress, and Wikipedia notes attacks on democracy by some; adherents are split.

direct-votes.rationale: Plebiscitary support and direct appeal to the people are defining features, though the sources frame it as a leader-centred strategy.

workers-councils.rationale: Neopopulists marginalise organised labour and rely on unorganised followers, so council-based rule is contrary to them.

right-to-secede.rationale: Inferred from nationalist, centralising leaders; not documented.

natural-rulers.rationale: Not addressed; the leader's charisma is stressed but no doctrine of natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Not addressed directly; leaders used force against insurgents while criticising violence, so split.

war-builds-character.rationale: No source ties neopopulism to a glorification of war; the answer is a mild inference from its focus on economic crisis-solving rather than martial virtue.

separate-church-state.rationale: Inferred from religious constituencies courted by some neopopulists; not documented.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Not documented; even religious-leaning neopopulists do not generally propose scriptural law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Neoliberal neopopulism shrinks the economic state but relies on state power to push reform; privatising courts and defence is not documented.

military-superiority.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; split.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Right-wing neopopulists in Europe lean toward it while Latin American cases appeal to a heterogeneous mass; split.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Weyland describes neopopulism as appealing to a heterogeneous mass of people against elites, not as a class-conflict theory.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Market-oriented programmes with only targeted relief do not aim at equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred from extractive, investment-friendly policy; the sources note mining expansion but not indigenous rights.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The sources say nothing about colonial reparations; inferred from the leaders' pro-creditor, pro-West economic stance.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not addressed; nationalist and personalist focus makes it unlikely.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Market-oriented thinking is inferred to tolerate self-interest; the sources do not state a moral claim.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The sources do not say whether duties outrank rights; neopopulist leaders stress citizen equality yet override rules, so this is a neutral guess.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Inferred from pro-extraction policy such as Fujimori's mining sales.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Fujimori's later family planning drive complicates this, so this is a weak inference.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Neopopulism is organised around modernising through market reform and exports.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Technological disruption is not discussed in the neopopulism literature, so no side can be inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: Body and mind enhancement is outside the 1990s reform-and-leadership literature on neopopulism.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed; personalistic rule is inferred to disfavour algorithmic replacement of the leader.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from security orientation.

restore-past-order.rationale: European right neopopulists invoke it while 1990s Latin American cases promised modernisation, so split.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Weyland shows leaders abandoned campaign promises and adopted market reform when it worked, a pragmatic stance that treats results as the test.

direct-action.rationale: They mobilise support at elections and through direct appeals but not through street direct action; inferred.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not addressed; leaders used transgressive means to impose reform.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Contrary to a modernising market programme.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: A market-reform programme depends on specialisation and wage employment, so abolishing the division of labour is inferred as rejected.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Market allocation with targeted relief, not need-based distribution.

production-for-use.rationale: Market economy with profit, as in reform programmes.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Neopopulist neoliberalism treats profit as legitimate returns.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Contrary to leader-centred plebiscitary politics aimed at a heterogeneous mass.

taxation-theft.rationale: Neoliberal neopopulists raised revenue and kept the state; libertarian claim rejected by inference.

harm-principle.rationale: The sources never state a liberal harm principle for these leaders, whose record mixes market liberalism with emergency rule, so it is neutral.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Not addressed; leaders appealed to the people as a whole yet stress individual citizen equality, so split.

conscription.rationale: Military service policy is not covered by Weyland or the glossary, so there is no basis for a side.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not addressed; plebiscitary leaders prize votes.

state-as-business.rationale: Business-style efficiency rhetoric appears with neoliberal reform but no source states citizens-as-customers; split.

positive-liberty.rationale: Targeted relief existed but the philosophy is market-liberal; inferred.

media-academia-power.rationale: Right neopopulists attack media and academic establishments as part of anti-establishment rhetoric, though not documented for the 1990s core.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not addressed; mainstream neopopulists do not generally claim this.

organic-representation.rationale: Weyland says neopopulists bypass organised bodies in favour of direct support.

total-state.rationale: Neoliberal neopopulism aims to shrink the state and privatise.

national-rebirth.rationale: Leaders presented themselves as saviours rescuing the country from crisis, which Weyland ties to proving charisma.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Neopopulism is defined by domestic leadership and crisis politics, not expansion, so a mild rejection is inferred.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Personalistic loyalty to a leader exists but not feudal oaths; inferred.

bound-labor.rationale: Binding farmers to land contradicts the liberalised labour and land markets these reforms created.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: A postmodern epistemic claim absent from neopopulist writing; the leaders' technocratic reform stance points mildly against it.

universal-morality.rationale: Moral philosophy is not addressed in the sources, so adherents are treated as neutral.

single-common-good.rationale: Not addressed; some appeals to the unified people but also pragmatism.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Zionism is outside the neopopulism sources, so no position is supported.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora return rights do not feature in the neopopulism sources.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is not part of the neopopulist programme described in the sources.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Neopopulists marginalise worker organisations and favour business-friendly corporate governance.

school-vouchers.rationale: Market-oriented reform is inferred to favour choice, but the sources do not mention vouchers and Fujimori's education reform met union resistance.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fujimori's programme aimed to hold spending to current revenue, and adjustment was fiscally orthodox.

economic-freedom.rationale: Market-reforming leaders linked liberalisation to prosperity, though they curtailed political freedoms; inferred.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not addressed; personalist but legalistic orders.

force-without-un.rationale: Foreign policy is barely mentioned in the sources; neutral.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The sources do not address faith versus reason; leaders courted both technocrats and religious constituencies, so neutral.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: European neopopulists support welfare chauvinism; weak inference elsewhere.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Targeted emergency programmes were often work-linked and neoliberal in spirit; inferred, not documented.

class-collaboration.rationale: Neopopulism rejects class conflict, appealing to the unified people and also courting business sectors.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Heritage institutions are not discussed; a mild rejection is inferred from nationalist cultural appeals.

dominated-front.rationale: Neoliberal leaders aligned with international financial institutions and the West.

workers-nation.rationale: Not addressed; they marginalise worker organisations.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Gender roles in law are not covered by the sources; neutral.

ban-interest.rationale: Neopopulist leaders such as Menem and Fujimori ran market stabilisation programmes that liberalised finance and depended on credit markets, which excludes banning interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Contrary to the leaders' appeal to a broad mass and to democratic law; no source supports it.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Neopopulism denies a class-instrument state, seeing the state as a tool for the leader and the people.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Fujimori's policy opened mining and extraction; inferred for fossil fuels.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Anti-immigrant stances in neopopulist parties imply assimilation; inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: Some right neopopulists voice it; Latin American core does not. Split.

proportional-representation.rationale: Plebiscitary leaders favour strong executives over party-based systems; inferred.

national-mission.rationale: Spreading a national model abroad is not a neopopulist theme in the sources; neutral.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Structural patriarchy claims are not part of neopopulist discourse; mild rejection inferred.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Anti-elite, anti-establishment discourse is a defining feature, with outsider leaders attacking cronies and traditional parties.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: No support in sources; contrary to equal citizenship appeals.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Fujimori granted amnesty and leaders resisted accountability; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Shrunk the state strongly but kept social emergency programmes; split.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: No source discusses mixed marriage; disagreement is assumed from the leaders' broad appeal across heterogeneous electorates.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Citizens counted as equal ("one citizen, one vote") per the glossary, though less central.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Settler-colonial framing is outside the sources; mild rejection inferred from nationalist rhetoric.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Religious personal-law debates are outside the Latin American neopopulism literature.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Conversion law is not discussed in the sources.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A South Asian issue absent from the neopopulism sources; mild rejection inferred from pro-market stance.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: School religion policy is not in the sources; neutral.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrine opposed to the market-capitalist stance of neoliberal neopopulists.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Leaders sought legitimacy through direct popular support and elections.

trade-surplus.rationale: Export promotion was central but mercantilist aim is not documented; split.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced removal of minorities is not part of the documented programme; mild rejection inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Not addressed; they rely on state coercion.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The sources do not say whether leaders favoured banning parties; neutral.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: A republican theory not discussed in the sources; neutral.

separated-powers.rationale: Weyland describes limited respect for institutional rules and concentration of power in the president; Fujimori closed Congress.

vanguard-party.rationale: Leaders are anti-organisational and distrust disciplined parties.

priority-to-poor.rationale: They courted the unorganised poor with targeted programmes but did not make poor-first law a principle.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Privatisation logic and property titling inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labour flexibilisation weakened unions and the presidents curtailed strikes.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The sources frame poverty as crisis and adjustment effects, and do not blame population growth; neutral.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Some right neopopulists claim so; Latin American core does not. Split.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Fujimori's 1992 self-coup and emergency measures drew mass support.

party-controls-media.rationale: Not stated; leaders courted media but formal control is inferred as rejected.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party control of the army is not in the sources, and neopopulist leaders build personal rather than party vehicles; mild rejection inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed; anti-elite rhetoric might support it.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: European neopopulists oppose EU integration; weak inference.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is not covered by the sources; neutral.

clerical-rule.rationale: No source discusses clerical rule; disagreement is assumed from the secular, leader-centred character of these governments.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Revolutionary defeatism has no place in the neopopulist sources and clashes with leaders' nationalist appeals.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Art censorship is not discussed; neutral.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Menem and Fujimori sought re-election and constitutional changes to allow it.

recall-officials.rationale: Not addressed; plebiscitary but not recall.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliance policy is not discussed; Menem and Fujimori cooperated closely with creditors and the West, so a mild rejection is inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Banning rentals contradicts the market-reform housing and property logic.

people-in-arms.rationale: An armed citizenry is not discussed; leaders relied on professional security forces, so mild rejection inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Appealed to the rural poor but no moral claim; neutral.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National division is not a topic in the neopopulism sources; neutral.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Cultural relativism is not addressed in the sources; neutral.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Curriculum on sex education is not covered; mild rejection inferred from socially conservative leaders like Menem.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed by sources; adherents differ by country so neutral.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; neutral.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship rules are not covered by the Latin American neopopulism sources; neutral.

minority-language-support.rationale: Language policy is not covered; neutral.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Religious exemptions are not covered; neutral.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Millian social-conformity claims are not covered; neutral.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: They accepted IMF and creditor obligations and sought to restore creditworthiness.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Economic independence arguments belong to dependency theory, which neoliberal neopopulists rejected, so mild disagreement is inferred.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Fujimori after 1992 convened a constituent congress; this is inferred only from general plebiscitary leanings, so low.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Weyland records authoritarian measures justified by crisis, but adherents do not state it as a doctrine; inferred.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Aid duties are not covered by the sources; Weyland notes international lenders funded relief programmes, but no stance is stated.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons policy is not covered by the sources.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Plebiscitary personalistic leaders are elected directly.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Neoliberal reformers favoured sound money, while personalistic leaders resist constraints; split.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial concessions are not covered by the sources.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A Marxist debate unrelated to neopopulism.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental precaution is not addressed; pro-extraction, pro-growth policies suggest mild disagreement.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance guarantees are not covered by the sources; neutral.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Annexation law is not covered by the sources; neutral.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Church-state relations are not covered; mild rejection inferred from leaders' cultivation of religious support.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Personalistic leaders are partisan political figures.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Special-region arrangements are not covered by the sources; neutral.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Divine descent for a ruler has no place in plebiscitary politics based on popular votes.

character-from-environment.rationale: Nature versus nurture is not covered by the sources; neutral.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Weyland says leaders limited respect for rules but not as doctrine.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is outside the sources; neutral.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed-regime theory is not covered; plebiscitary leaders concentrate power in one office, so mild rejection is inferred.

leader-cult.rationale: Personalistic leadership implies heightened public honour; not directly documented.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family court policy is not covered; neutral.

land-redistribution.rationale: Neopopulist market reformers aimed at titling and investment rather than breaking up estates, and the sources never mention land reform; inferred from the market programme.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return is outside what the neopopulism literature discusses, so there is no basis for a side.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred: the Latin American core leaders did not make irredentist claims, and nothing in the sources endorses them.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred: leaders ran secular electoral politics and no source suggests criminal penalties for leaving a religion.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred: no neopopulist source supports compulsory dress for women.

common-currency.rationale: Menem's convertibility pegged the peso to the dollar, but the sources do not discuss shared currencies, so adherents are split.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred from the leader-and-nation focus; the literature does not discuss pan-ethnic union.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred: centralising plebiscitary leaders would not grant self-governing minority institutions.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Diaspora strategy is not discussed in the sources, so neither side is supported.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Weyland defines populism as a political strategy relatively autonomous from socioeconomic conditions, which is inferred to cut against materialist history.

ban-cartels.rationale: Deregulation is documented but antitrust is not; inferred that breaking up economic power was not a goal.

no-bailouts.rationale: Neoliberal austerity favours it but personalist leaders favoured crony business sectors, as Weyland notes with privatisation; split.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Weyland describes leaders with limited respect for institutional constraints who treated popular support as mandate; inferred, not stated as doctrine.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred: quotas are not part of the market-reform programme.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Fujimori's government abandoned import substitution and reintegrated Peru into world trade.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred: liberalising reform treated open trade as the goal and labour standards as burdens.

moral-incentives.rationale: Market reform relies on material incentives and a capitalist model.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: These leaders fought armed insurgents and sought change through elections.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inferred from anti-elite, anti-establishment rhetoric; nobility is not discussed.

history-own-civilization.rationale: School curriculum is not covered in the sources, so no side is supported.

patriotic-education.rationale: Nationalist strands of neopopulism favour patriotic education, but this is inferred.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred from right-wing neopopulism's rejection of identity-based redress.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred from the sound-money orientation of neoliberal reform.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Weyland shows neoliberal neopopulists regarded market reform as the way out of crisis, implying capitalism can adapt.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not part of the neopopulism literature, so no stance is supported.

delink-world-market.rationale: Fujimori's government reintegrated Peru into world trade and finance and removed exchange controls.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Inferred: a theory from Marxist-Leninism with no place in these leaders' discourse.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Not discussed by the sources, and adherents are split.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Neopopulists were willing to override constitutional rules but also promulgated constitutions; split and undocumented.

elective-rulers.rationale: Neopopulist leaders gained office through elections and drew legitimacy from them.

minority-veto.rationale: Plebiscitary, majoritarian leaders bypass organised minorities and veto players.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred: leaders who limited institutional rules would not endorse a right of removal.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Weyland describes leaders concentrating power in the president, and Fujimori closed Congress in 1992.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics is not covered; neutral.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not covered; neutral.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Not a documented theme; targeted relief existed but without an obligation doctrine.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Neopopulism mobilises people directly behind a leader.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred: leaders used mass media to build support and would not criticise it.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A critical theory these leaders do not hold.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Fujimori and Menem integrated their countries into the world economy and rejected dependency framing.

native-born-offices.rationale: Not discussed in the 1990s core, though nativist parties may favour it.

party-own-road.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist question outside the neopopulist context.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Weyland notes international financial institutions funded social emergency programmes, which these leaders welcomed.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Irredentism is not part of the 1990s Latin American neopopulism sources; neutral.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred: not a theme of the programme.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Constitutional anti-fascism is not covered; neutral.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Right-wing neopopulism tends to condemn communism and fascism together; inferred.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from nationalist and anti-establishment currents in right neopopulism.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not covered by the sources; neutral.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not covered by the sources; neutral.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Not covered by the sources; neutral.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Fujimori relied on the armed forces after 1992 but the literature does not make this doctrine; split.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred: not part of targeted relief or market reform.

filial-duty.rationale: Not covered by the sources; neutral.

office-by-exam.rationale: Not discussed; leaders attacked cronies but their civil-service views are not documented.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Fujimori eased limits on investment and capital flows and privatised to attract foreign buyers.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is not covered; neutral since leaders such as Menem were publicly Catholic yet divorced.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred from personalistic rule, which sets aside delegate-style accountability.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Fujimori created a private pension system in 1993, though the page I read does not mention it; this is inferred from neoliberal reform and rated low.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Market reform and property titling favour individual tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from leaders' limited respect for legislative constraints.

single-official-language.rationale: Language law is not covered by the sources; neutral.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Investment-friendly liberalisation opposes restrictions on foreign ownership.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from right neopopulism's rejection of identity-based redress.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred: market-reform programmes seek consumption and growth.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred: not a focus and leaders faced domestic insurgents themselves.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Spheres-of-influence intervention is not covered; neutral.

corporate-influence.rationale: Weyland notes privatisation gave benefits to powerful business sectors, so these leaders did not see lobbying as a problem.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Some right neopopulists restrict NGO funding, but the 1990s core says nothing.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Population incentives are not covered by the sources; neutral.

job-guarantee.rationale: Market reform shrank state employment, per Fujimori's cuts to public employment.

democratic-peace.rationale: Democratic peace theory is not covered by the sources; neutral.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred: leaders asserted authority as the people's mandate.

non-intervention.rationale: Sovereignty norms are not covered; neutral.

industrial-unions.rationale: Weyland says neopopulists marginalise unions, so they would not promote a particular union structure.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Right neopopulists sometimes scapegoat groups; not a defining feature of the core.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred: not part of the programme.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Government transparency is not covered; neutral.

local-production.rationale: Export promotion and integration into world trade oppose localism.

informal-organisation.rationale: Neopopulists are anti-organisational and personal-vehicle based, which differs from informal affinity groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Not discussed; nationalist streams might say yes, others accept IMF programmes.

religious-nation.rationale: Not covered by the Latin American core; neutral.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred: these leaders cooperated with the West, but ritual submission is not stated.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Trivially accepted within a market society.

defeat-communism.rationale: Fujimori fought Shining Path and market leaders opposed state planning; inferred as an attitude to communism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Privatisation of telephones and utilities alongside public provision suggests a mix; inferred.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Market capitalism was embraced as the route out of crisis and to growth, per Weyland.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: not part of the programme.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from shrinking of the state.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is not part of the sources; mild rejection inferred from outward-looking market reform.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with internal nations are not covered; neutral.

majority-settlement.rationale: State-sponsored settlement is not part of the documented programme; mild rejection inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Contradicts the market reform and anti-organisational character.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Neopopulist neoliberals accept capitalism; a third way is not their stance.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Not covered by the sources; neutral.

holocaust-denial.rationale: No source connects neopopulism to it; inferred as rejected by mainstream adherents.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not documented for these leaders; mild rejection inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Weyland records autocratic acts, such as Fujimori's closing of Congress, but adherents mostly claimed popular mandate; split.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Not documented for these leaders; mild rejection inferred.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Not relevant to these leaders; inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Religious-law rebellion is irrelevant to the secular electoral strategy of neopopulism.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Neopopulism is plebiscitary but anti-organisational, not participatory in this sense.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Right neopopulism rejects this framework; inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from socially conservative right neopopulism.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The Wikipedia article says neopopulist movements sometimes reject the left-right label, and Weyland shows leaders combining policies across it.

alienated-labor.rationale: Not a theme of market reformers.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Anti-Muslim policy appears in some neopopulist parties, but not the Latin American core; split.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Inferred: authority is drawn from the people's support.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not covered by the sources; neutral.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not covered by the sources; neutral.

social-market-economy.rationale: Neopopulists combined market reform with targeted social programmes but never endorsed a social market framework, so the answer is unclear.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Security-minded leaders relied on the armed forces.

rich-first.rationale: Neoliberal logic of growth first; inferred, not stated.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Fujimorism did see Keiko Fujimori succeed politically, but the programme does not endorse hereditary office; inferred.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Market finance and stabilisation packages rely on interest-bearing credit, contradicting mutual interest-free banks.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Menem and Fujimori adopted IMF-backed adjustment and Weyland says international financial institutions pushed these reforms.

property-franchise.rationale: Neopopulists seek mass support; a property franchise would cut against it.

domination-women-nature.rationale: An ecofeminist claim not covered in the sources; mild rejection inferred.

reification.rationale: A critical theory outside the programme.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Not covered by the sources; leaders cultivated media, so mild rejection inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Leaders exceeded rules at times but also governed by decree; split.

racial-franchise.rationale: Neopopulism seeks mass support among all.

open-government-data.rationale: Not covered by the sources; neutral.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Not covered by the sources; mild rejection inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Not covered by the sources; mild rejection inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred: personalistic leaders bypass deliberative bodies.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Not covered by the sources; neutral.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Weyland notes leaders benefited powerful business sectors, which cuts against this claim.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not covered by the sources; neutral.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Leaders relied on state security forces.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Neoliberal states relied partly on private effort, but the emergency programmes were state-run; split.

term-limits.rationale: Leaders sought re-election and weakened limits; inferred as their view.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred: not part of plebiscitary strategy.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not covered by the sources; neutral.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Not covered by the sources; neutral.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Not covered by the sources; neutral.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred: not part of the programme.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Not documented for these leaders; mild rejection inferred.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not covered by the sources; neutral.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Not covered by the sources; neutral.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not covered by the sources; neutral.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred: market returns to capital accepted.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred: leaders used force against insurgents.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Not covered by the Latin American core; neutral.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from socially conservative right neopopulism.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: A feminist theory claim; mild rejection inferred from the socially conservative right wing of neopopulism.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Not covered by the sources; neutral.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Not part of a pragmatic reform strategy.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not covered by the sources; neutral.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred: neopopulism is state- and leader-centred.

god-not-male.rationale: Not covered by the sources; neutral.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not covered by the sources; neutral.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Not covered by the sources; neutral.

independent-unions.rationale: Weyland says neopopulists distance themselves from unions, so they are not supporters, but independence is not discussed; split.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: A socialist definitional claim; neopopulists reject worker-power projects, so mild disagreement is inferred.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Law 23.696 names water and sanitation (Obras Sanitarias) among enterprises subject to privatisation.

second-chamber.rationale: Legislative structure is not covered; neutral.

municipal-property.rationale: Contrary to private property and market model.

family-wage.rationale: Wage-setting norms are not covered; neutral.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Deregulation generally is documented but drug approval is not; mild agreement inferred.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not covered by the sources; neutral.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not covered by the sources; neutral.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not covered, and the 1990s cases predate widespread internet use; neutral.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Neopopulism aims at the whole people; inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: Not covered by the Latin American core; neutral.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Not covered by the sources; neutral.

free-public-college.rationale: Fiscal restraint suggests mild opposition to free tuition, but the sources do not discuss it.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Environmental taxes are not covered; mild rejection inferred from pro-growth policy.

capital-controls.rationale: Fujimori's reforms removed exchange controls and eased limits on capital flows.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Not covered; refusal of war orders is contrary to leaders who relied on armed forces.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Weyland says labour flexibilisation weakened unions and neopopulists kept away from them.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Targeted programmes existed, but tax credits are not documented.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Fiscal discipline yes; binding rules limit leaders; split.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Not covered; the leaders accepted existing creditor rules, so mild disagreement is inferred.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Neoliberal neopopulists used the state to push reform.

sacred-nation.rationale: Not covered by the Latin American core; neutral.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not covered; fiscal restraint suggests mild disagreement.

internal-colonialism.rationale: A dependency-theory concept; mild disagreement inferred.

public-service-media.rationale: Not covered; mild disagreement inferred from privatisation and media cultivation.

farm-price-support.rationale: Fujimori removed subsidies and price controls.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not covered by the sources; inferred as mild agreement with the equal-rights majority.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Not covered by the sources; inferred as mild agreement with market property rights applied equally.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Not covered; mild rejection inferred from centralised national rule.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not covered; pro-growth extraction policy suggests disagreement.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Not covered; mild agreement inferred from a security-and-order focus.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not covered by the Latin American core; mild agreement inferred from anti-immigration neopopulists.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Weyland describes weakening unions through labour flexibilisation; opposition to compulsory membership is inferred.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Leaders won elections, but did not define democracy; inferred.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Not covered; the 1990s cases predate widespread internet use.

women-suffrage.rationale: Not covered; mild agreement inferred, since neopopulists seek mass electoral support.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Not covered; mild disagreement inferred, since leaders courted religious voters.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Not covered; mild disagreement inferred from state-shrinking reform.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Planned economies are opposed by neoliberal neopopulists.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Not covered; mild disagreement inferred from centralised rule.

simple-living.rationale: Neopopulist reform aims at growth, consumption and investment, which contradicts voluntary simplicity.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Weyland documents emergency anti-poverty programmes aimed at the unorganised poor as the neopopulist substitute for universal or union-mediated welfare.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Weyland defines neopopulism as direct, unmediated support from unorganised followers and says leaders marginalise unions, parties and other organisations.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Market-oriented technocratic neopopulism had no ecological or land-bond doctrine, so this is inferred from its modernising, growth-first programme.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred from the constitutional, plebiscitary form of 1990s Latin American neopopulism, which attacked institutions but did not formally claim a licence to kill suspects; later right-wing variants differ.

close-ties-china.rationale: Menem, Fujimori and Collor tied their reforms to US-led lenders and markets, so leaning on China is inferred to be against the grain.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The sources describe no kin-minority policy; inferred from the domestic, economic focus of Latin American neopopulism.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Its programme privatised state assets and promoted private ownership, from which a compensation-to-all view is inferred to be rejected.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred from its market-liberal economic creed; its leaders were nonetheless willing to override individual and institutional constraints, hence low.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred: Fujimori-style reform simplified taxes and favoured broad-based revenue; the sources do not discuss consumption taxes directly.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The reforms cut subsidies, price controls and tariff protection, which fits the principle even though privatisation in practice often favoured connected buyers.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Neopopulists claimed to speak for the whole people against organised groups, so denominational blocs are inferred to be unwelcome.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Anachronistic for this strand; nothing in the sources addresses ancestral values, and the modernising reformers and later nationalist variants would split on it.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the secular-liberal, modernising stance of the Latin American leaders, though some allied with conservative Catholics.

national-resource-control.rationale: The programme privatised state firms and utilities and welcomed foreign capital, which runs against national control of resources.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred from the neoliberal reform programme of Menem and Fujimori, which accepted market outcomes and attacked organised distributive interests.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred from the liberalisation of capital markets in neoliberal reform, which is hostile to levies on finance.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Not addressed for the Latin American strand; later right-wing neopopulists differ on race.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no shared stance on natural-law claims.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Not addressed; neopopulist reformers focused on privatisation, not automation.

multipolar-world.rationale: Not addressed; the strand was oriented to Washington-backed reform, but no stance on world order is stated.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred from the neoliberal economics the strand adopted, which values goods by market demand rather than labour.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Not addressed; leaders appealed to the nation, but adherents have no shared view on its link to workers.

material-over-identity.rationale: Not addressed; the strand is not defined by left strategy.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred from the strand's market liberalisation under a personalistic leader, not party-led socialism.

missingStatements.text: Social spending should be targeted at the poorest rather than provided universally.
missingStatements.rationale: Weyland documents emergency anti-poverty programmes aimed at the unorganised poor as the neopopulist substitute for universal or union-mediated welfare.

missingStatements.text: A president facing a political crisis may close the legislature and rule directly.
missingStatements.rationale: Weyland reports that Fujimori's April 1992 closing of Congress drew his highest popular support, and that plebiscitary leaders show limited respect for institutional rules.

missingStatements.text: Political parties and interest groups stand between the people and their leader and should be bypassed.
missingStatements.rationale: Weyland defines neopopulism as direct, unmediated support from unorganised followers and says leaders marginalise unions, parties and other organisations.

notes: The term is contested: Latin American critics dispute that Menem and Fujimori were populists at all (the bait-and-switch reading), and the Wikipedia usage covers right-wing movements whose economics Wikipedia describes as contested. The profile follows Weyland's political definition. Most answers outside economics, labour and leadership are low-confidence inferences.
